title: Connection and Timeout Management
learning_outcomes: Explain how connection and timeout management affects an API contract or implementation.
Apply the key ideas from client and server timeouts to a concrete API example.
Identify one failure, security, or compatibility risk and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on connection and timeout management in caching, conditional requests, and performance. You will connect client and server timeouts to a concrete API contract decision, inspect a small example, and decide what evidence proves the behavior is correct.
content.why_it_matters: Connection and Timeout Management matters because API consumers depend on predictable behavior even when clients, servers, networks, and stored data evolve independently. Applying client and server timeouts deliberately reduces ambiguity, makes failures easier to diagnose, and gives tests a clear expectation.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Caching and validators can reduce work and prevent stale reads or lost updates, but cache policy must protect sensitive representations. In this lesson, treat “Connection and Timeout Management” as a design or implementation decision: name the expected behavior, identify its boundary, and verify it with a representative request or test.
